title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection of latency regressions and add rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We've seen intermittent latency regressions slip past canary detection when changes affect tail latency under low traffic patterns. This PR improves the performance canary auto-detection heuristics and introduces a rollout guard controller that prevents automated rollouts when certain regression signatures are detected. Summary of changes: (1) detector: add EWMA-based baseline with tail-aware aggregation and a new percentile-shift detector to capture regressed p95/p99 under sparse samples; (2) sampling: introduce adaptive synthetic load probe that increases sample density when variance is high; (3) rollout guards: new controller that evaluates canary signals across latency, throughput, and error budget and blocks automated promotion if any signal exceeds configured thresholds; (4) metrics: add k/V cache hit-rate and scheduling-queue-length metrics to the canary dashboard to help root cause classification; (5) infra/ci: new perf-canary pipeline job that runs end-to-end against a canary cluster and emits signal artifacts to S3 for reproducible analysis; (6) docs: add operational playbook and config knobs for teams to tune thresholds. Testing: unit tests for detectors; integration test that injects synthetic latency and verifies the guard blocks rollout; e2e run in staging with canary traffic for 48 hours. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature-flagged guard in staging for 72h, monitor perf signals and run quick rollback playbook if false positive rate > 10% on p95 alerts, then schedule gradual opt-in to production for low-risk services over two weeks. Risks and mitigations: false positives on highly bursty workloads (mitigated by adaptive sampling and opt-out per-service), small-sample statistical noise (mitigated by minimum-sample thresholds and EWMA smoothing), increased CI runtime (mitigated by running heavy e2e only on nightly runs). Related: ENG-1123, ENG-1189. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] docs updated [x] staging verification completed.

release_notes: Improves performance canary sensitivity to tail latency regressions and adds a rollout guard controller that prevents automatic promotion when latency/throughput regressions or related signals are detected. Includes new config knobs and an operational playbook.
review_comments: Priya Nair: Overall looks good. Two requests: make the default guard thresholds conservative, and add a short-circuit to allow manual override from the console.
Aisha Patel: Addressed both requests — thresholds default to conservative values and added a consoleOverride flag with audit logging.
Evan Zhao: Left a comment on detector.go about potential numerical stability in EWMA when weights are small, please add a guard.
Aisha Patel: Added clamp for smoothing factor and a comment with references to the original paper; added unit test for extreme smoothing values.
Marco Li: Ran staging canary for 48h against messaging-service, observed no false positives and approved.
Priya Nair: Approved after verifying RBAC changes and docs.

rollout_plan: Feature-flagged in staging for 72h -> monitor signals -> opt-in to production gradually over two weeks for low-risk services. Manual override available in console with audit logging.
notes: This change is part of a multi-PR effort to harden canary detection. Follow-ups planned: centralized signal store, UI refinements for guard reasons, and per-service auto-tuning of thresholds.
